newsitem.title: USA: Child murder prompts Nevada casino curfew on kids.
newsitem.headline: Child murder prompts Nevada casino curfew on kids.

text.p: A curfew prompted by the rape and murder of a 7-year-old girl will ban unaccompanied children from casino amusement arcades in America's gambling capital, officials said on Wednesday.
The crackdown coincided with Nevada being named for the second year the most dangerous state in the country, based on murders and other violent crimes.
It also comes at a time when Las Vegas casinos are trying to attract a more family-oriented clientele, by adding diverse attractions to amuse children while parents gamble.

The Board of Commissioners for Clark County, which includes the city of Las Vegas, voted on Tuesday night to bar anyone under the age of 18 from casino arcades between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. on weeknights and between midnight and 5 a.m. on weekend nights. The curfew takes effect on Sept. 13.
Atkinson Gates, chairwoman of the board, proposed the curfew after the May 25 murder of Sherrice Iverson at the Primm Valley hotel casino in Primm, Nevada, while her father was at the gaming tables.
She told the Las Vegas Review-Journal in an interview that it was the reponsibility of elected officials "to fix what is broken" in the system.

The slain girl's mother, who was not at the casino when her daughter was murdered, has sued the Primm Valley hotel casino. The suit by Yolanda Manuel, filed on Tuesday in Clark County District Court alleges that there was a lack of supervision for children at the hotel, despite its all-night amusement arcade.
The suit seeks unspecified damages from the hotel's parent company, Primadonna Resorts, which owns half the Las Vegas casino New York, New York.

"It knew children would be accompanying adults, and they made the place attractive to kids," said Manuel's attorney Barry Dunn. "Nevertheless, the arcade section and other areas where children played were not adequately monitored by Primadonna personnel."
Aaron Cohen, a spokesman for Primadonna Resorts declined comment on the suit but said the company would comply with the curfew ordinance.

Jeremy Strohmeyer, 18, has been charged with sexual assault, kidnapping and murder in the Iverson killing. He was seen on security cameras following the girl in an amusement arcade at the hotel-casino at around 3 a.m.
The girl's body was found in a stall of the women's restroom in the arcade. A friend with Strohmeyer said the youth went into the restroom and was there for about 20 minutes.
In an affidavit, detectives said Strohmeyer molested the girl and then snapped her neck.
The hotel said the unsupervised girl had been stopped three times by Primadonna security guards and released to the custody of her father, Leroy or her 14-year-old brother.
Strohmeyer was extradited from California earlier this month to be arraigned in the small Nevada town of Jean, some 30 miles south of Las Vegas.
According to state crime statistics compiled by the independent publishing company, Morgan Quitno Press, Nevada is the most dangerous state in the United States.
The rankings, now in their fourth year, are based on six basic crime types -- murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary and car theft.
State officials argue that the figures do not reflect the fact that Nevada attracts a huge number of tourists and most crimes involve residents of other states.
